message: Two independently selected targets (#18 and #72) have now reproduced the same process-level failure: persistent network memory changes the second query, but the reconstruction collapses toward alphabetic/lexical residue rather than a compact relation-level trace. Treat this repetition as evidence about the memory→reconstruction→query process, not about either target. Without assuming an implementation, determine whether the current problem-formation machinery can admit that process-level residual. If admitted, devise a prospective comparator in which the existing lexical projection is frozen as baseline and a learner-authored semantic trace/crystal must improve a later query, retrieval, or problem-formation consequence on fresh returned data. Preserve source provenance and residual disagreement; WITHHOLD if the process-level residual cannot be lawfully formed or the candidate cannot beat baseline. Do not treat this mentor description as target-binding, evaluator return, truth, or promotion.
purpose: Expose a cross-target returned residual and let Minerva decide whether/how to form and test a process-level semantic trace abstraction.
